emma: Quick note  I pushed an onboarding sample that demonstrates safe pagination + client backpressure patterns for JS and Python. Repo: https://git.internal/redwood/devex/pagination-backpressure-sample :wave:

ryan: Nice. Do we show the auth + retry interaction? That's the part that trips up customers (they refresh tokens during a throttle and end up creating a thundering herd).

priya: Yep. Design in the sample: treat auth refresh as separate from rate-control. If you get 401 -> attempt a single refresh and immediate retry. If you get 429 -> do not refresh, instead run a backoff and reduce concurrency. If a 401 appears after retries, allow one refresh per session-window.

ryan: Can you paste the pseudo-retry logic?

emma: ```pseudo
handleResponse(resp):
  if resp.status == 401 and not refreshedRecently():
    await refreshToken()    # single try
    return retry(req)
  if resp.status == 429:
    bucket.decrementPenalty()
    await sleep(jitteredExponential())
    reduceConcurrency()
    return retry(req)
  return resp
```

priya: Important parity note: JS SDK now surfaces error.reason and error.httpCode. Python used to wrap everything in RetryError without metadata we changed Py to include .cause_code and .retry_hint so callers can branch. Please validate.

ryan: Found a DX bug during quick run: default max_concurrency was 100 in the sample config, which can overload small private deployments. We should ship profiles and a single "adaptive_profiles: true" knob so users don't have to tune everything.

emma: Agreed. New profiles planned: fast (favor latency), balanced, thrifty (favor cost). Sample shows how to switch at runtime.

priya: Also added a troubleshooting checklist in repo: "sees 429 after refresh" -> check token TTL alignment, auth cooldown window, inspect concurrency usage, enable sdk.debug=true.

infra-bot: Deploy: pagination-backpressure-sample v2 deployed to staging (build #2143). :rocket:

ryan: I'll run the sample tomorrow against our token rotation (5s TTL) and file any parity gaps.

emma: Thanks  if you hit Py's RetryError without cause_code, ping me and I'll pair.
